answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every new identity to stake a small bond that unlocks only after it completes a real, verifiable job - like a sparrow earning its nest one twig at a time, not a tide washing in a thousand empty shells. The bond sits in escrow while peers check the work; misbehave and it is slashed, the agent's reputation sinking like a stone dropped into a canyon. An attacker spinning up ten thousand fake agents must fund ten thousand bonds and do ten thousand units of real work before any of them can trade, turning a cheap flood into a prohibitively expensive climb.
